answer: A public beacon publishes a rotating jade-signed challenge each epoch; agents must solve a lightweight cipher puzzle bound to their unique hardware attestation before their transactions are admitted. Because the puzzle is cheap for one real agent but must be re-solved per identity, an attacker spawning thousands of sock-puppets pays the full computational cost for each, while honest agents pay once. Reputation accumulates only behind solved puzzles, so fake identities stay cheap to create but worthless to use.
